summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after abnormal outpatient labs showed severe hypernatremia and metabolic acidosis, but repeat testing in the emergency department revealed these were likely lab artifacts. His blood glucose remained elevated at 453 mg/dL, attributed to recent corticosteroid injection for hip pain. He was asymptomatic with stable vital signs, normal cardiac and pulmonary exams, and no evidence of infection or acute cardiac ischemia. His insulin regimen was adjusted upward slightly to manage steroid-induced hyperglycemia. He remained stable throughout a brief observation stay, with glucose improving to 196 mg/dL by morning. He was discharged home with instructions to monitor blood sugar closely and follow up with his primary care physician.
